targetText: The slave is sold once and for all; the proletarian must sell himself daily and hourly.
summary: Comparing labor across modes of production: the slave is sold once as chattel, while the proletarian must sell labor power continuously.
explanation: Engels highlights the structural difference between slave and capitalist modes of production: the ancient slave was property of a single master, whereas the modern wage laborer is free from individual bondage yet economically compelled to sell labor power to the capitalist class as a whole.
